thread.title: Under Armour remains committed to opening flagship Fifth Avenue New York store

author: Holden Wilen
title: Under Armour remains committed to opening flagship Fifth Avenue New York store
text: – Reporter, Baltimore Business Journal Aug 7, 2018, 2:37pm EDT Under Armour Inc. says it is committed to opening a flagship store on Fifth Avenue in New York next year despite the sportswear maker's ongoing restructuring effort. Baltimore-based Under Armour announced in 2016 plans for a new brand house to open inside the space formerly occupied by the iconic FAO Schwarz toy store. The 53,000-square-foot store on the first floor of the General Motors building would put Under Armour's interlocking "UA" logo in front of thousands of tourists from all over the world. Amid a decline in North American sales, Under Armour (NYSE: UAA) has implemented a restructuring plan that will end up costing more than $200 million this year but is expected to save the company money in the long term. CFO David Bergman said during a July 26 conference call with analysts that a majority of the items in the restructuring plan, which was expanded in the second quarter, are related to long-term contract, facility and lease terminations. He said the plan would affect a "few stores in North America" that the company was not originally looking at. An Under Armour spokeswoman said "there are no changes" to the company's plans to open its Fifth Avenue store in 2019. Boston Properties , which has a majority ownership stake in the General Motors building, declined to comment. New York real estate news site The Real Deal estimated in 2016 that Under Armour's lease at the FAO Schwarz space will cost $30 million annually. As it keeps an eye on spending, Under Armour backed out of a deal that would have made it the official on-field outfitter for Major League Baseball. The decision reportedly saved Under Armour $50 million. But Under Armour's latest comments affirm that the company is not reversing course on its plans for New York. Under Armour has 80 brand houses globally, including 15 in North America. Locations include Harbor East; Michigan Avenue in Chicago; and downtown Boston. Apple Inc. (NASDAQ: AAPL) currently occupies the FAO Schwarz space. The tech giant set up a store there temporarily while its glass cube-topped underground store undergoes a renovation. Apple's renovations are supposed to be completed this fall and Under Armour expects to take over the lease in 2019. Under Armour CEO Kevin Plank said the Fifth Avenue location was chosen because of its notoriety. FAO Schwarz closed the store, which was used in the famous piano-playing scene in Tom Hanks' 1988 comedy "Big," in 2015. "We want to build one of the most breathtaking retail experiences there," Plank said when announcing the store in 2016. President Patrik Frisk addressed Under Armour's strategy for its store during the July 26 call with analysts. He said the company sees an importance in having brick and mortar stores and may accelerate its pace of building across the globe. "We do believe that in every part of the world, there is a retail component that’s needed to actually meet the consumer as the consumer expects that 360 degree or omni-channel experience with the brand," Frisk said. "We’re getting smarter about what’s actually going on in our stores in terms of how the consumer is shopping and then what the consumer expectation is."
